utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pranjkovic [sic]. Would you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is Franjo Kovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: It doesn't make much difference. I had proposed earlier on that there should be a closed session, but there is no need for that. I consulted my colleagues, and we came to the conclusion that it can be held in open session, but from time to time we will move into private session when we mention the names of protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Again, good morning, Mr. Kovac. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning to all. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. Yesterday we played a videotape, that is, 20/4, and we

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [redacted], and I suggest that this be moved into evidence. Of course, if the Prosecutor is not opposed to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No objection. It is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Good day to all present here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You are going to introduce yourself to the Court now. You are going to give us your name and surname, your date of birth, where you live and where you work.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I am Franjo Kovac. I was born on the 4th of October, 1959, in Butici, the municipality of Novi Travnik. I live with my wife and two children in Santici, BB Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please tell whether you have a house in Santici?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I do have a house in Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it built before the war or after the war?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It was built after the war, and until the war, it was only started.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did you work in 1993?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: In 1993, I was employed in Novi Travnik in a trade company. I was involved in trade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How long did you work there?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I worked there until the conflict broke out in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did you spend more of your time: in Novi Travnik, in your native village, or in Santici?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I lived in Santici, but I spent more time in Novi Travnik or, rather, in Butici at my parents' place because I had transportation problems so I would spend more time in Novi Travnik rather than at home in Santici. I would come there only when I was supposed to get my salary or on Sundays when I would not work, when I would have a day off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So due to your work, you spent more time in Butici than in Santici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When you would come to Santici, and I'm talking about 1993, to whose house would you come if your house had not been completed by that time? Please just wait a minute and answer my questions slowly. Now go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I lived in the house of Nikola Omazic because my house had not been completed yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who else lived with you in this house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: My wife and one child.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did the inhabitants of Santici know you well because you did not live in Santici?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, just the neighbours, the closest neighbours that helped me when I built my house because my house was built with the help of my neighbours up to the first floor. It never went any further. So we know each other. They helped me out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: As you were in Novi Travnik, did you do any guard duty from Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mean to say rarely?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: As you're not from Santici yourself, did you have a uniform and did you have a rifle?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, I didn't have a rifle or a uniform, and I wasn't in Santici much. I was in Novi Travnik and Butici at my parents' place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you tell us what you did during the first conflict, that is to say, where were you during the first conflict on the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I remember where I was. I was free, I had a free day, and I -- and Anto Bralo and myself decided to go to cut firewood in the wood around him because I had this motor saw and I deal in trade, and we went off in the morning with Mirsad Osmancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And who is Mirsad Osmancevic?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Mirsad Osmancevic is a neighbour. His house is a little above my own, and I went with Anto Bralo's brother, his nickname was Bica, I don't know his name, he was killed, and we went to Kruscica, that is to say, above Kruscica, to cut wood in the woods above Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you went to cut wood. Could you tell us who Mirsad Osmancevic was? Was he a member of any army?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I knew him well. We were friends and visited each other, and he would go fairly often to some sort of training. He was in the army and would go to some sort of training.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What army?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It was the Muslim army. But what function he performed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he train others or not?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, he did something of that kind, some sort of training for others. Whether he was a commander of any kind or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is he in the BH army today?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, he is. I heard that he is and that he is an officer today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that he was a member of the BH army. Do you consider that the BH army existed or not, or was it only the army of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Serbian republic?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Today it is the army of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but previously there was an army ... How shall I say? I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, yes, there are two armies, the one of the Serbian republic and the federation.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That is what was introduced into the constitution, although there are different interpretations of it. Tell us, please, what you did on the 15th of April, 1993, and where were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, I was at home because I had come a day before that from Novi Travnik, I came home, because I had to do some work on my house. I had to build something onto my house, one of the structures, and so I was at home that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You say that you worked in Novi Travnik, and the 15th was a working day, so how could you have been in Santici that day?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: How I came to be in Santici that day? Is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, I had a free day. I was free that day, so I went to Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you move off from your house anywhere that day?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I needed some petrol for my motor, I had no gas, so I had to go to Vitez, and I went by bicycle because I had no car, so I went to Vitez to get some petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who sold you this petrol at the petrol pump in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: The petrol pump attendant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: At that petrol pump on that particular day, was Nenad Santic there?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, he was, and he gave me the petrol, tanked up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And did he work at that petrol pump?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, he did work at the pump.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The first conflict, do you remember whether anybody's shed was set fire to at Santici or anybody's house shot at Santici in your neighbourhood? Tell me.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, when I came from Kruscica, that was on the morning of the 20th, my wife told me that -- her name is Katica, that Drago Josipovic's shed was burnt, set fire to, and that his house was damaged, the facade and the tiles, and there was also a window that had been shot through and pierced by a bullet on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was his house damaged during the second conflict as well?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you give us a full sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, his house was damaged in the course of the second conflict too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Let us now move on to the 16th of April, 1993. Could you please tell us how you experienced that day? Do you know what happened that day?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I do. In the morning between the 15th and the 16th, that is to say, on the 16th in the morning, we were woken up by -- I was woken up by shooting. I jumped out of bed, I woke my wife up, and I said, "There seems to be a lot of shooting going on." We jumped out of bed. I took up my child -- I took up my child, as I say, and my wife, and we went out of the house and we moved towards Anto Bralo's house. As it's an open space, we were not able to take -- we had to -- we were not able to take the road but took to the fields.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you took a short-cut to Anto Bralo's house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What time was that in the morning?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It was about 5.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How far is your house from Anto Bralo's house as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: You mean Nikola Omazic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Nikola Omazic's house is about 50 metres away, 50 to 60 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And you say that you went there to Anto Bralo's house with your wife and child.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you meet Anto Bralo there?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was at the entrance door. He met us by the front door. So that I took my wife inside, and I stayed outside in front of the entrance talking to Anto Bralo and we saw Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, let us take first things first. You met Anto Bralo, you took your wife and child inside, and who did you see from there?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I saw Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: At the crossroads towards Nikola Omazic's house, Anto Papic and Anto Bralo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, the two of them were talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, Anto Bralo and I moved towards them. We took the road going around. There's a little fence there --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you speak slower, please?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, there was a sort of hedge, and this was a little kind of shelter; otherwise, it's an open space. So we took the path -- the round about way, and when we came to the crossroads, Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic moved along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did they start walking along the road before you arrived?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't want to follow them, so we went towards Anto Papic's shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they went in one direction and you went in the other.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: We went in the other direction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You went towards the shed?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were their backs turned to you as you left?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did they see you? Could they see you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, they saw us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And now please tell us what you did when you went to the shed. Tell us the sequence of events.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: There was a lot of shooting, and anyone could have been hit by a bullet. We went to Anto Papic's shed because it was the safest place there. It was about 40 metres away. We went over there, Anto Bralo and I, because that was the best shelter from bullets. After some time, Hasima came by, Hasima Hasim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Please give us her name and surname.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is the last name [redacted]

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, now I would like to move into private session because we are going to mention names that are protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, we will move into private session. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You just said now, Mr. Kovac, that -- actually, that Ljubo Cerkez was there just in passing. Tell me about that morning. Where were you going that morning? We're talking about the 16th. Did you see Drago Josipovic that morning, except when he and Anto Papic brought the Muslims that we talked about?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, we were moving in that area all day. That was Anto Bralo's house, and Anto Papic's house or, rather, the shed of Anto Papic was there too. And Bralo and I had a task or, rather, we had agreed on something with Marija Papic, a neighbour. We were supposed to go and feed her cattle, because she was a bit further away from Bralo's house. We went there to milk the cows and to feed the cattle, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So you went to milk the cows in the morning?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What time was that?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: That was around 10:00, 10:00 or 11:00. Sometime during the day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Since we said that some Muslims came to Anto Papic's house, do you know who were the people who were in Anto Bralo's house that day?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: When we talked to Marija Papic, when we said we were supposed to go milk the cows, at Anto Bralo's house there was Marija Papic, Ljubica Skuro, Simo Vidovic, Jozo Santic, Finka Bralo with two children, I already mentioned Ljubica. She had a child too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Ljubica who?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Ljubica Skuro.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And her name was different afterwards, wasn't it? Is that Ljubica Milicevic?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's Ljubica Milicevic, but Skuro is a nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That day when you saw Drago Josipovic, what did he look like? What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic was wearing blue trousers, a blue shirt, and he had a camouflage vest, and he had a rifle. He was carrying a rifle too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We talked about village guards earlier on.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In this area, from Anto Papic's house to the road or to the house of Drago Josipovic, was -- or, rather, Nikica Grebenar, was he there on guard duty with you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No. I know Nikica. Nikica's job was the following: He was supposed to assign people to guard duty. He was involved in making out this list, who was supposed to go where.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why did he not have guard duty?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Because he had a work obligation. He was a trade inspector, and I was involved in trade, so we always communicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Nikica Grebenar have a rifle?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No. No, he did not have a rifle, till he got a rifle from Nenad Santic. That rifle was Fahran's rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Give us his last name, too.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It was Fahran [redacted] rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So Nenad Santic gave him this rifle?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, Nenad Santic gave him a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: He gave it to Nikica Grebenar?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, to Nikica Grebenar. And since Drago Josipovic did not have a rifle and since he was friends with Fahran [redacted], and then they were talking to Drago Josipovic, and Drago was supposed to get this rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he talk to Drago or Nikica Grebenar?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Fahran talked to Drago that Nikica should take this, and then Drago talked to Nikica, and that's how he got this rifle, and that's how Drago Josipovic got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I don't know if you understood this. Are you sure that he talked to Nikica Grebenar or Drago Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Fahran talked to Drago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'm putting the following question to you: Did he talk to Nikica Grebenar about handing over this rifle, because Nikica Grebenar was the one who gave out different assignments. Did he talk to Nikica Grebenar or Drago Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: He talked to Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you talk to Nikica Grebenar?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: You mean Fahran [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, I mean Fahran [redacted]

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: He talked to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, did Fahran [redacted] talk to Nikica Grebenar about having this rifle handed over to Nikica?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Because Nikica told me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Nikica work on building your house and were you good friends?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: We were only good friends through work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You were good friends with Nikica Grebenar and he told you something. What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: He told me that the rifle was taken away from Fahran [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who took it away?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Nenad Santic took it away from him. The gun was given to the village guards so that the -- but in order to prevent the rifle from going further on, to some other place, then Fahran asked Drago Josipovic that Drago go and ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No. Well, not Drago. Did you talk to Nikica Grebenar or Drago? Please tell me.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: To Nikica Grebenar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And who gave Drago Josipovic the rifle?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Nikica Grebenar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Okay. Right. We are talking about the 16th of April, 1993. Tell me, who else came it to Anto Papic's house, who from the ranks of the Muslims? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I know. In the afternoon --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I think that you don't know those last names because you were not born there.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right. Especially from the left-hand side. [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps we should move into private session, because we're going to mention a few names again. Private session. Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Private session. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We wish to apologise for the slight delay. We may now resume our proceedings. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, do you know Drago Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know his mother?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I know her very well. She is a very ill woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us, on what terms were you with her, between his mother and you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, we were on very good terms. Because I was away from home, his mother often spent the night in my house or, rather, in Nikola Omazic's house. She spent a lot of time with my wife, especially after the first conflict. She was afraid to be alone, so she often came over to my wife and spent the night with her. Drago also came and we visited each other and we built my house together so that I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why did Drago Josipovic's mother come to your house? Why was that?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It was because Drago Josipovic's wife was full-time employed, she worked for a private businessman, and she simply could not help her enough, so that she would come over to my wife, and my wife is with her to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Drago also help her?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Drago was very devoted to his mother, and whatever she needed, Drago did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you used to see Drago Josipovic and his mother?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him in his garden quite often. Because she was ill, she suffered from cancer, Drago always did things in the garden and took care -- took care of their vegetable garden, and he even prepared preserves and conserves together with his mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. You said that you worked in Novi Travnik. Mr. President, I should like to show a document to the accused, so will the usher please -- will the usher please also take this document from me and give it to the Chamber and show it to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D22/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, have you read this certificate?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is it true that you worked for Novotehna in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Until the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, until the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you have your work booklet? Do you have it with you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is it. So if the Prosecution does not trust the certificate, they can check it in his work booklet, employment booklet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that you knew neighbours living near your house.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you please tell us who were those neighbours; to begin with, Muslims.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. My next-door or, rather, the neighbour who lived across the street was Cazim Ramic, with his family, that is, his wife Zilka and two sons --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you just tell us the households?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Right, households.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Does his son also have a house of his own?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he does. There is also -- I just can't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it perhaps Zenur Ramic?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, quite right, Zenur Ramic is the house to the right, and there is also -- and another house is Mirsad Osmancevic's. They're all along our street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That is, from Anto Papic's house towards the road.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is [indiscernible translat ion] [redacted] house there?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, [redacted] house is across Mr. Osmancevic's house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us if any of these persons living near Anto Papic's house and near yours, was any one of them killed on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, nobody was killed on our street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And as you turn towards the road?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: As you turn towards the road, in the house to the right, the one which was killed, that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Fahran.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Fahran [redacted].

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No. Fahran was his first name. I can't remember his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. And do you know of anybody else?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But were the houses closer to Anto Papic's house or to the road?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, these houses are nearer the road because near Anto Papic's house are only these two houses, Mirsad Osmancevic's and Nail's house and the one that was across from my house, across the road from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will the usher please show the aerial photographs to the witness, and I shall then ask him to mark those houses?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D23/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you please take a marker?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: A marker?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, or a pen. Something. And will you please mark the house? Have you found it? Do you see your way around that map? You can turn it around if it's easier for you.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, I think I've got my bearings now. Whose house?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could the other witness's microphone be switched on, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you put an "A" next to [redacted] [redacted] house, please? Mr. Kovac, perhaps it would be better to take another copy. I think this is a clearer photograph, so perhaps it is better.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I can try.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I mean, it has the same houses. Perhaps you can look at both of them. You think this one is better.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: This one is better.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, look at it, find your way around it, and then take the other photograph. Yeah, will you please compare the two? Look at both of them, and I think it will be simpler for you to find your way about them.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, right. I see. Yes. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Right. Now, on the second photograph, which is clearer, will you please mark [redacted] house and put an "A" next to it -- no, no, no. On the other one, on the other photograph, because it is clearer. That is why. Will you place it on the ELMO so that we can see? [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [NO TRANSLATION]?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Counsel Susak --

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I don't really know where they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: First of all, we don't have any translation, [redacted] 2 [redacted] 3 [redacted] [redacted]. If you don't mind, for a few minutes, we will move into a private session. In any case, I wonder whether it is so crucial if the witness is unable to locate that particular place. It is not very crucial because we have so many --

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I can, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will move on to other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have been asked by various people whether we should go into private session or not, and my colleagues confuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We are going, yes, into private session, first of all, but then again, as to the location of this particular house, if the witness is unable to locate it, I mean, I think we can move on to other questions, if you agree. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you told us that those houses were not set on fire, that only one was set on fire and that that happened on the 17th of April. Whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: That was the Zilko's or, rather, Cazim Ramic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Zenur Ramic's house, does it still stand?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it does. It still stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Mirsad Osmancevic's house, does it still stand?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. There are some Ramics living in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. On the 16th of April, did you enter Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, yes, I did, but it was only in the evening, in the evening, late afternoon, and with Anto.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Whom did you see there?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: In Anto Papic's house I entered. I was looking for cigarettes, and I was given them. There were Cazim Ramic, with Zilka with two sons, with three children; Mirsad Osmancevic with three children, and baby, and his wife. There was Anto Papic's sister and wife with two children. There was [redacted] [redacted]. There were a number other people but I did not know them. They were refugees, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Were these people accommodated? Were they in the rooms, or in the passage, or in the rooms?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: They were both in the rooms and in the passage, because all these rooms are very small. So they were also in the passage, and there was also a kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: These persons, did they come in and go out in the way that not all of them were in those rooms all the time?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. They could go out at their own responsibility, of course. I mean, they had to take care that no bullet hit them, but they could go out and come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know if Muslims came out and moved around, and some of them came to Niko Omazic's house or to Anto Bralo's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. I heard it from my wife. I did not see them, but I heard from my wife that Hasim's wife came to Finka Bralo. I asked about my wife, so as to call her son who was in Vitez, and my wife agreed. So they went to my home or, rather, to Niko Omazic's house and she made a call to Vitez. That is what my wife told me. I heard it from my wife. I did the not see that personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Right. Now we are talking about the 17th of April, 1993. Will you tell us if you saw Drago Josipovic that day or not?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I saw him quite a number of times. Even Drago spent the night in Niko Omazic's house. That is my place. And Dubravka Santic was also there with her three children. So it was better for them. Drago and I, we spent the night together. Drago did not go to his home because his house was damaged, rather, at the time of the first conflict, and even at the time of the second one. It was hit several times. So it was safer for him to spend the night at my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know -- were you with Drago Josipovic after that? Was he in Anto Bralo's house with you, or back in his house, or did he ever go back to his house? Do you know something about that?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: On the 17th, in the morning, we went to Anto Bralo's, and we sat down with him and had coffee and were talking about where we would go, to move around or not. We agreed that Drago Josipovic should go home and feed the pigs and that Drago and I should go to Marija Papic to feed the poultry. So we did. Drago stayed behind, and I heard that later on he went to feed the pigs, that is, to his yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, it was around 10.00. In the morning, I mean? Well, it was roughly about 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you see him in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were you moving about those houses or not?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, together we were at Bralo's and at Anto Papic's, but those were roughly our movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So it was throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Since the Muslims were in Anto Papic's house, would you know when was it they left the house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I heard from Anto Papic that Anto took them to the road or, rather, it was UNPROFOR which was allegedly to take them or that is what Anto, I think, said to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That is, you know that only because Anto Papic told you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I did not see them leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You did not see them?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't because we were at Marija Papic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you see Drago Josipovic go from that house to his -- from your house to his house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: From my house to his house. No, I don't know that. I know that he left from Bralo's house because we both left Bralo's house together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, but did Drago Josipovic go home?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, but he went there from Anto's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But did you see him leave?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because we left before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You left before him. Will you tell us -- so you saw Drago Josipovic on the 16th and on the 17th. Where were you mobilised, if you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I was mobilised. Not only me, but we were all mobilised four days after the war, that is, on the 19th. A courier came and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you tell us which 19th of what?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: 19th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Which year was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who came to fetch you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, it was a courier, and all he said was we should all get together and leave. So we did. All of us who were on the road, we crossed the road to the other part of the road, that is, to the road to Rovna, and we all met there, and went to the line in Safradini.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was in that group?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It was Anto Bralo; Drago Josipovic; and then another; Dragan Santic from across the street, from another street; then Ivo; then Nikica Grebenar. I didn't know those people. I met them later on when we were at the defence line already. That is a new Nikica. I didn't know his brother. There was also Nenad Santic. Well, these are the people I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. The Prosecutor gave us a certificate of the Croat Defence Council of the Vitez Brigade, and that certificate is of the 15th of April, '94. The certificate was issued subsequently, at a later date, after the mobilisation. It says that you were a member of the HVO, that is, of the HVO Vitez Brigade as of the 6th of October -- 16th of April, '92. Just wait. I haven't put my question yet. This certificate also says that you were wounded on the 16th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: At Krtina-Mahala?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us when was it that you were mobilised in the Vitez area for the first time?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: The first and the last time I was mobilised was on the 19th of April, '93, but before that, I think, out of spite, they simply reported me, those village guards. I was supposed to be on village guard, and I think somebody put my name down on the list and that is how I think I got on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Just a moment. Wait. So in other words, are you saying that somebody told on you? But were you registered to Santici as a person with a residence there?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No. Nobody had done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But were you issued the papers in Novi Travnik, because you were a member of army formations or village guards?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, I was in Novi Travnik but because I was still working there. That is how papers got from Novi Travnik, because I was not registered down there, so that I could not get any papers down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I suppose the Prosecution will ask you about that. I'm not going to bother you any more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I wonder whether other Defence counsel intend to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, other counsel do not have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. My name is Franck Terrier. I'm one of the representatives of the Prosecution, and I would like to ask you a certain number of questions. First of all, with the assistance of the usher, I would like you to have a look at the certificate that was mentioned by Mr. Susak.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P368.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise. I just wanted to draw your attention to one point regarding this certificate. Please take note on the Croatian text and the date on the English translation. The translation was done by the Office of the Prosecutor. My colleague, Mr. Susak, gave the exact date, which was the 15th of April, 1994, whereas the English version, the date is the 15th of April, 1995. Also, the numbers relating to that document above the date, after the illegible part of the Croatian text, it is 09/94, whereas in the English text it is 09/95. So please take note of that if you will. We don't know if it is just a typing error or something else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is true that it seems the translation, which is a rough translation and not the final translation, seems to contain a mistake, but I wanted to base my objection on the original, where the figures are very clear, even for a person who couldn't speak Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: There is no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I will then repeat what I've just said, very briefly. I agree with what Mr. Radovic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, you had enough time to have a look at this document?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Had you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Whether I'd seen it before? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you hear about it? Were you aware of the existence of this document?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, I did not know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: According to this document dated 15th of April, 1994, you were wounded on the 16th of September, 1993 when you were fighting within the Viteska Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise? In which unit were you fighting?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Which unit, you mean? I was the 1st Battalion, the 1st Platoon, and the 3rd Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you give the names of the officers, your superiors?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I just had one officer. I didn't meet the others. That was my commander, deputy commander, in fact, and his name was Jozo Plavcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You will agree that in this document it is said that you are a member of the Viteska Brigade and that you have been a member of this brigade since the 16th of April, 1992. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: According to this document, that's what it says, but I wasn't in Vitez. I was in Novi Travnik, because Novi Travnik paid out those shares to me as of that date, as of the 16th of April, 1992, and not Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: A few moments ago when you answered a question asked of you by Mr. Susak, you explained the reason why this date had been mentioned in this document. I do apologise, but I didn't really understand your explanation. Could you please repeat what you said to Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Could I what?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: A moment ago Mr. Susak asked you why this date of the 16th of April, 1992 had been mentioned in the document, and you explained why you were registered, without knowing it, on the guard list. Could you please go back to this explanation and be more precise?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Because somebody told on me, denounced me, out of spite, out of hatred, because I did not go on these guard duties, and so they tried to make me a part of those guard duties, tried to make me do the duty. But as I wasn't there, well then ... So I didn't, in fact. They didn't know about me, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: If I understand you well, but I'm not completely sure I understand you well, all the inhabitants of Ahmici had to do guard duty or other military tasks within the Viteska Brigade -- did I understand you well? -- which would explain why you are mentioned as a member of the Viteska Brigade since the 16th of September [as interpreted], 1992, because you were denounced?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, not from the 16th of April, 1992. I was a member as of 1993; that is to say, the 19th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I would like for the usher to give to the witness Exhibit 353 of the Prosecution, and more precisely, page 78 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On this page, page 78, I will draw your attention to the number corresponding to the name, rather, corresponding to the number 3306, and I would like you to confirm if this is your name.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On this line on the right-hand side of the page, you can see a signature. Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On this very same line, it is indicated that you were a member of the HVO from the 8th of April, 1992, till the 1st of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I can't explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I will also draw your attention to the fact that you signed this book, that your signature is opposite the dates which are indicated.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, it seems logical to think that when you signed this book, you knew what these dates corresponded to. Sir, can I ask you, what is this green notebook that you've just opened to find some information, I guess?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: A record of employment, and I'm looking at it to see my years of service, because the 26th is mentioned here, and I wanted to see whether anything was different in my booklet, employment booklet, but it has nothing to do with what we have here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Sorry. If you don't have any explanation to give to us, then we'll move to another subject.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us that at that time, that is, at the beginning of 1993, you were working in Novi Travnik and that usually you would stay in Novi Travnik and that you would go to Ahmici only rarely. Could you tell us if your family, that is, your wife and your child, were living on a permanent basis, so to speak, in Ahmici or Santici?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: In 1993? Everything was normal. Nobody provoked them or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how often you would come back from Novi Travnik to Ahmici? Was it every weekend, every month, or did you come back more frequently?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Sometimes once weekly, sometimes every fortnight, so I would go back every month, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us that your family lived in Nikola Omazic's house. Was there more than one Nikola Omazic living in Santici or Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: As far as I know, there is another Nikola Omazic, yes, and that is my father-in-law, who is in Vitez, and he has a house in Santici. But there's another Nikola Omazic who lives at Zume, that is to say, above the road, the upper side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You said that on the 15th of April, 1993, you came back home with your family in Ahmici. Was there any particular reason for you to come back since it was on a Thursday and not during the weekend?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. It was payday. I had collected my salary and I was taking it home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Couldn't you wait until Friday or Saturday to do that?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, it could have waited, but I had a free day because I worked the Sunday. So if I worked the Sunday, then I can use that day when I need it, and I took a free day, I had already worked out my shifts, and as I say, it was payday, so I collected my pay and went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: For how long had you been working for this company in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Since 1987. I don't know the exact date. I have it, of course, written down in my record of employment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On the certificate that you were given a moment ago, it says that you've been working there since February 1993.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: '87 until the 7th of June, '93. Yes, because -- up until '93 because all the roads were blocked and I wasn't able to go to my place of employment; and as the war started in Novi Travnik a little later, broke out there a little later, these years of service were recognised for all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think there has been another error in translation which has nothing to do with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, sir, there were no particular reasons for you to come back to Ahmici that Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I shall repeat the question. According to what you have just said, there were no particular reasons for you to go back on that Thursday, instead of Friday or Saturday, as you would usually do, to go back to your village. You didn't want to protect your family against a potential incident, for instance? If I thought that this was the case, then I would be wrong; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: That's right, because I went to work and then I took my paycheque home, and I had to work on my house, I had to build up something in my house, and that was the reason: Because I brought back my salary, I had a free day, and I had work to do on my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: During the night of the 15th and 16th of April, 1993, unless I'm wrong, I heard that you were on guard duty during that night.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you have a certain duty to carry out during that night for the whole community?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, I had nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You had never done guard duty in Ahmici or Pirici while you were there?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Very little, almost nothing, not at all, and I remember the last guard duty that I did. It was two hours in the month of February with Anto Bralo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: During the morning of the 16th of April, 1993, you said that you were awoken by shootings, gunfire that you heard. Then you took your family in or to Anto Bralo's house. Why did you choose that particular house, Anto Bralo's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Because it was the nearest house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us why your family could not stay in that house, in Nikola Omazic's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Because it's not a well-built house and it's always safer to be with more families than alone, so those were the reasons. And my wife was afraid when the first conflict took place, so it was safer to go to Anto Bralo's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, how was Anto Papic dressed when you saw him for the first time that morning, on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Anto Papic was wearing a camouflage uniform. He had a camouflage uniform, both the bottom part, pants, and the upper part as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did he have some insignia or some patch or something on that uniform?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I don't remember him having any. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did he have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He had a rifle, an M-48. It's an old rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us that Drago Josipovic was wearing blue trousers and a camouflage jacket. On that camouflage vest, was there any insignia or any patch or anything?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I didn't see it. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He had an automatic rifle on his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you be more accurate as to the model of the rifle that Drago Josipovic had over his shoulder on the 16th of April in the morning?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It was what we call a Ciganka. It was an automatic rifle with a short butt.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In view of your military experience, what is that type of a weapon? How is this type of a rifle usually used?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: For defence. For self-defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Why was it that this rifle was particularly an indicated rifle for self-defence?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, what else could you use it for? You use it for defence purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Perhaps this seems a strange question, but can't a defence weapon be used also for an attack, as a weapon of attack? Now, you have military experience; that is why I am asking you that.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, of course you can use it for an attack if you need an attack. But if you have it for your defence, then it's for defence purposes. It depends what you use it for.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I see. Did you see around your house, that is, Nikola Omazic's house, or around other houses in this same place, in the vicinity, some soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any because there's some growth by the roadside, a sort of hedge, a hedge, so you couldn't see, although it is open space otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You said a while ago that intensive fire made you hide behind Anto Papic's stable. Do you know where this intensive fire came from and who it was aimed at?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, I didn't look to see what it was aimed at, but it came from all sides, so that we found ourselves behind Anto Papic's stable. I don't want to say that they were aiming at me or anybody else. Anybody could have been hit who happened to be passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you remember the place where you were when you met [redacted] and her husband Hasim? Where were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I was in front of Anto Papic's stable with Anto Bralo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, he did not say that he had met Fatima [redacted]. He said that they were behind Anto Papic's stable, that is, away from the road and away from the path taken by Fatima, and so I would like to make an objection so as not to confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Terrier, perhaps you could rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to do that, but it seems to me -- right. Well, this is a misunderstanding. So I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing Fatima [redacted] that morning and also her children and her daughter-in-law? You know who I am talking about.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I didn't meet them. They passed us by. But Drago Josipovic met them and Anto Papic did too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: How do you know that Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic met them? Did that happen in your presence?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Because they came up to us and said to us that -- they said that [redacted] had died because they were at the junction there while we were going on to Anto Papic's house. They took the right side of the road, so I could see them and they could see us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You said a while ago, in answer to Mr. Susak's question, you gave the names of some persons who had found shelter at Anto Papic's. Did you enter that house on that day, on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No, I did not. We were only moving in front of the house. As for the house itself, we entered it only in the evening. Anto Bralo and I, we came to the hall of Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us about Anto Bralo who was with you in front of Anto Papic's house? Could you tell us, what was he wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: He was wearing the same uniform that I saw him in the morning, that is to say, the camouflage jacket and the olive green trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did he have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, he had an M48 rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it correct as this translation follows, in Anto Papic's house, in two rooms, nine metres square each, there were over 30 persons, as you said, and another witness 38 persons. And there were near those 30-odd persons, there were three individuals in military clothes and armed. One of them was you. Wouldn't you go in to provide guards, to guard those refugees, those sheltering people? Am I clear? Wasn't it to prevent those people who had sought shelter to disperse, to scatter around?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I did not understand this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I shall be happy to repeat it. I'm asking you to tell us if it is true or not. In Anto Papic's house there were those two rooms, two nine square metres each. In them there were over 30 persons, as you said, or 38 persons, according to another witness, all of them Muslims. Near those 30 or 38 persons there were, at least at some points of time during the day, three persons wearing camouflage uniforms or, rather, all Croats, all three of them armed. So my question is as follows, rather, my interpretation which I put to you is that following that, does that not mean that these three armed Croats had the duty to stand guard over those 30-odd Muslims so as to prevent their dispersing, so as to prevent their departure either to Rovna or any other direction, to prevent their leaving the house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: They could go out whenever they wanted to and wherever they wanted to go. As for the house of Anto Papic, as far as I know, I did not see a single camouflage uniform except for Anto Papic and Anto Bralo. They had uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Why did not these individuals get to a separate place by leaving this area and going to Rovna?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Because that was the nearest to them. In order to go to Rovna -- it's a longer trip to Rovna. This was closer and they got along very well. They could have gone to Anto Bralo's house too, because it was Hasim and Hasim's wife that were amongst the first to arrive, and their daughter-in-law, and all the others came too because they felt safer when they were all together rather than if they dispersed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, witness, but my question is: On the 16th of April, 1993, they could have, all together, perhaps even with your help, gone to Rovna or in the direction of Rovna, and they would have been, evidently, quite safe there. So at the place where they were, they were not altogether safe. Their security was not certain.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Their safety and security was 100 per cent because no one touched them and no one mistreated them. Even as much as possible, we gave them food. We also gave their children clothes. They were free to go wherever they wanted to, as far as we, their Croat neighbours, were concerned, and they could go wherever they wanted to, because they were not threatened there anyway. So that is why they felt safest there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Right. In the night between the 16th and the 17th, you spent the night in your house, Nikola Omazic's house, and Drago Josipovic was with you. That is what you told us. It seems, therefore, that then that night, between the 16th and the 17th, Nikola Omazic's house was safer than the other one?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No. No, it wasn't safer, but since there were so many people at Anto Bralo's house, and Anto Papic's, why wouldn't they be staying at Nikola's too? Again, it is easier for them not to be too crowded, not to have that many people packed together. That's why we went to Nikola Omazic's place, that is to say, to my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On the 16th and that night before the 17th, where was Drago Josipovic's family, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: In Rovna, at Slavica Josipvic's parents. That is to say, his mother and his wife Slavica. That's what I heard from certain neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you know when Drago Josipovic's family went to Rovna?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: No. I did not see them, and they probably left when the shooting began.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you hear, if you did not see, in what way did the Josipovic's family get to Rovna? What kind of means of transportation did he use?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us a while ago explaining the presence of Drago Josipovic in Nikoka Omazic's house with you, that his house had been damaged. Did you see with your own eyes the damage inflicted on Drago Josipovic's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: After going to the front line -- and I did not say that today, Dragan only told me, but I didn't see this myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you describe the damage that you saw with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I did not see it with my own eyes. I did, after the first conflict, I saw it with my own eyes, but after the second conflict, no, I did not see it with my own eyes. I only heard about this from Drago, that his house had been damaged again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic didn't tell you anything about that, to tell you that his house had been hit, and you do not know anything else, any more details about it, do you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I don't know anything. I just know that he told me that his house had been damaged by rifle bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I should like to ask you my last question. Why is it that spending the night in Nikola Omazic's house, why did you spend it there rather than stay closer to Anto Bralo's house in order to look after your family? You told us there were lots of people there but, nevertheless, don't you think that they could have let you into that house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, why would we create any problems, and why would there be too many people in one house when there was no one practically in the other house except for me, and Drago, and Dubravka, and my wife with the children? It was probably more comfortable up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could one say that if you spent the night in Nikola Omazic's house rather than with your family, it was because during the night, between the 16th and the 17th, you absolutely had no fears for the safety of your family which was staying with Anto Bralo's?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I shall repeat the question. Since you spent that night, between the 16th and the 17th in Nikola Omazic's house rather than with your family, does that not mean -- can one not conclude that you did not fear for the security of your family there that night, you were certainly that your family was quite safe in this Anto Bralo's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: The 17th, in the evening, I was in the house with my wife. Could you please repeat your question once again, please? I can't understand what you're asking me to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, do you want me to ask the question once again? I should simply like to -- 368 be tendered to the Tribunal. We shall give the translation -- a better translation of that document when it is finished and with all the revisions and corrections that were indicated by Mr. Radovic. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Terrier. Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In response to the Prosecutor's questions, you say the people could go out of Anto Papic's house and come back and go out and come back again?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And before, when I asked you, you said that some Muslims would go out of this house of Anto Papic's and that they communicated with your wife.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, my next question: On the 16th of April, did Muslims go out of Anto Papic's house and come back in?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, they could have because Hasim's wife herself, she went out and she sent to Anto Bralo's house. So they were not forbidden to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat my question. Did they go out and come back in?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did they do that all day?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, all day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In response to the Prosecutor's question and also in response to my question, you said that evening you and Anto Bralo came to the house of Anto Papic. It was in the evening; wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us the reason why you came to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Anto Bralo and I did not have any cigarettes. We came to Anto Papic's house, and we asked someone for cigarettes. However, cigarettes were given us to by Zilka, that is to say, Zilka Ramic. She gave us about ten cigarettes in a box. Together with Anto Bralo, I managed to see all of those who were present there in the house of Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that on the 16th of April, you and Anto Bralo went to milk cows?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you do that on the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. We did that until we went to the front line, that is to say, until the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was this milk intended for the Muslim children who were in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It was intended for them and for our own families. No one made any distinction between the children. It was taken to Bralo's house and it was taken to Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know who brought food supplies to Anto Papic's house that day and whether Muslim children got clothes as well?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. As for milk, it is Anto Papic who brought it in most of all, and he also brought in clothes. He took care of them more than anyone, and he also came to our place, to my wife, and then to Finka Bralo's and then clothes were given for the children, for all the children, for all the Muslim children at Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So these Muslims who were in Anto Papic's house, you said that they got out, they would go out, and you said that they had a high degree of communication with you, the neighbours who were there, for example, with your wife, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They would go and make phone calls to call Hasim's wife's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So Muslims would come to Bralo's house even before you and Anto Bralo, in the evening, stopped by at Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was that a sign that there was friendly communication between you?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: There was always this friendly communication and then that's the way it was too. We were friends and we would spend time together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about the reason why you came to Nikola Omazic's house, and you said that there were two reasons for this. First all, that you got your salary and also that you had workers who were working at your own house.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I came home. It was a regular thing to do, because I had a day off. At the same time, there was construction going on at my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How old was your child then?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: At that time four.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Had you known that a war would break out in your immediate neighbourhood, would you have relocated your child, a minor, and your wife from Nikola Omazic's house?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I would have, by all means, like anyone else, if I had known.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you this certificate and that book too, that you were a member of the army from the 16th of April, 1992, but you said that you were first mobilised on the 19th of April, 1993, that is to say, after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Tell us, did you hear how it happened that other people came to be on this list? Were you really on this list because you were a member of the armed forces, or was there another reason for this?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Please repeat your question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you your signature showing from when you had been a member of the HVO. However, Mr. Kovac -- Mr. Kovac, you said you were mobilised on the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: 1993. 19th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How come you are on this list then?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Because somebody had entered my name. Somebody had entered my name on the basis of the census, so someone entered my name into these lists too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How come you signed this?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: I don't know how this happened. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And now tell me something else. You said that you mostly stayed in Novi Travnik. Since you were a member of the reserve force, did you get shares in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have these shares and I can prove this, but I haven't got these here with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Do you have any document showing that you became a shareholder?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you have this document?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Well, it's at my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you where it is. I'm not asking you whether you have it here with you.

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: It's at my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You're trying to tell me that you have a document showing that you obtained shares in Novi Travnik where you lived and where you worked on the basis of the fact that you were a member of the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is it possible for you to present this document to the Court?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are you going to submit this document to me as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: Franjo Kovac
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume there is no objection to Exhibit P368 being admitted into evidence, Counsel Susak, so it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, at the same time, I wish to tender D22/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection? Any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Admitted into evidence. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I omitted to tender the documents that were marked D7/6, and that is a Defence Exhibit of Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No. THE PRESIDENT: All right. So it is admitted into evidence. We don't have any questions for you, Mr. Kovac. Mr. Kovac, thank you so much for coming here to The Hague to give evidence in court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, are you going to call witness number 3, Pranjkovic, today or tomorrow, or what shall we do? Shall we go on with your list?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
