utterances.text: Mr. President, it is another witness, Katica Kovac, and then the Court is going to decide whether we are going to question her or not. I am neither for nor against, but I suggest that the Court decides whether we continue the questioning already today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, we go on today because we have a half an hour. Are you suggesting that we should move into a closed session for Mrs. Kovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No, I don't think that is necessary because I'm not going to be quoting which witness said what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I said so only because on your list, next to her name, there is also, in brackets, "(Closed session)." I don't intend to suggest that we should have closed session. In principle, all of our sessions should be open because of the need for trials to be fair and public. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I got a message from the registry, and that's why there's been a bit of confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Kovac. Would you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to all present here in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you introduce yourself to the Court? Could you please give us your name and surname and tell us when you were born and where, who you live with, and please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: My name is Katica Kovac. I was born on the 19th of November, 1962. I live with my husband and two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether you have a house in Santici?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. I built my house in Santici after the war. I lived in my father's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What's his name?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Nikola Omazic. The house is also in Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where your husband was born and where he is from?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: He was born in Bucici, the municipality of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he work there or not?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: My husband worked in a trade company called Novotehna, Novi Travnik. He worked there as a salesperson.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And until you built your house, you said that you lived in your father's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. For a certain period of time, we lived in Bucici. When we decided to build a house in Santici, then we moved to Santici to my father's house, Nikola Omazic's house, and my husband worked in Novi Travnik. He had transportation problems, so my husband would spend the night often in Bucici at his parents' place and he would come home only every now and then. You never knew when he would come home exactly because this depended on his work shifts and on whether he had transportation. I was at home with the child I had before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Did your husband ever register Santici as his place of residence?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: No, no. My husband did not register his place of residence in the municipality of Vitez. He had not made a definite decision yet with regard to his place of residence. Nobody knew him there. And all the mail, all the information he needed, he received in Bucici at his parents' place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You also said that very few people knew him.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, very few people knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did your next-door neighbours know him?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, Anto Bralo knew him best of all because he was our next-door neighbour and Drago Josipovic too because Drago would spend quite a bit of time at our place since his mother, who was very ill, would spend quite a bit of time in my house simply to keep me company because I was on my own with my child and so that I would not be afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Tell me, did you help Drago Josipovic's mother?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I would cook and very often we would have meals together, lunch, dinner, whatever, and I spent most of my time with Luca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Since Drago Josipovic's mother was staying with you, would Drago Josipovic stop by often?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Drago would come and ask us whether we needed something and we were in communication with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How come Drago Josipovic's mother would stay with you so often rather than at her own place?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: When the first conflict broke out between the Muslims and the Croats, the barn of Drago Josipovic was burned and also the house was damaged. Luca is an elderly woman and she was ill, so she addressed me and she stayed at my place. I helped Luca even before this first conflict because Drago Josipovic's wife had work duty and she was rather busy, and she did not have enough time to dedicate to her mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that Slavica Josipovic was too busy?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, Slavica Josipovic worked -- worked for a private individual and she had very many things to do, so she did not have enough time for her mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Drago have enough time for his mother?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Drago would spend a lot of time with his mother and he was very attached to his mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that Drago would come to your house.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When you would go up there, would you see them in their house or garden?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I would see Drago Josipovic very often in the garden and I saw them sitting there together and I had many opportunities of seeing Drago preparing food for the winter or cooking lunch or whatever because his mother was ill and she was not in a position to prepare food that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Where were you during the first conflict, that is to say, October 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: During the first conflict, I was at my own house -- in my own house, that is, and in the morning, when the shooting started, I was in my own house. The first thing that I heard was that Drago Josipovic's stable had been set fire to and that his house had been damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Frano Kovac [no interpretation].

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: My husband, one day prior to the conflict, went to Anto Bralo's to cut wood, firewood, for the winter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who went with him?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Anto Bralo's late brother went with them and Mirsad Osmancevic, our neighbour. They worked together and they took part -- they helped us build our house, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mirsad Osmancevic, do you know where his house is located? Is he a Muslim or not?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, he's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is his house standing today?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, who Mirsad Osmancevic is, if you know him? Has he got a wife, children?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you something about Mirsad Osmancevic. He is a Muslim by ethnicity, he has a wife, Saiba, and three sons. I know that he was a member of the BH army and that he went away from his house and would spend five, six, or seven days away from home, and this was his military duty. What he did, I don't know. I don't personally know that. I know that he was a member of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you happen to remember the 15th of April, 1993, and whether your husband was at home that day or not?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: In April, we started building our house, and on the 15th of April, my husband was at home because we had some work to do on the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Just try and speak a little more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I will. So my husband was at home on the 15th because we did some work on the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he leave?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, the shops are nearby, and we would buy all we needed in the shop nearby. I think my husband went to Vitez to buy some fuel because we used a motor saw and needed petrol for this saw, and he went to the petrol pump in Vitez to get the petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now we'll move on to the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where were you sleeping on the night between the 15th and 16th?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: In my own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How did you wake up, and tell us how you experienced the 16th of April? What was that day like?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, the 16th of April, in the morning, we were woken up by the sound of shooting. We got up and decided to move to Anto Bralo's house because his house is more sheltered than my father's house. So we ran across with our little girl to Anto Bralo's house. We went the shortest route to Anto Bralo's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: It is in a sort of depression and it has a basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And if you look at the level of Nikola Omazic's house and compare it to the level of Anto Bralo's house --

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, Anto Bralo's house lies lower, it is lower-lying, and therefore we were safer there. It is safer there and more protected than my father's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And you say that you, your husband, and who else?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: My son Mario.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you describe how you met Anto Bralo and what happened there when you met him and when you came there?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: When we came there, we found Anto Bralo standing in front of the house. I went into the house to Finka, his wife, and my husband stayed outside in front of the house with Anto, and they just said that they had seen Drago and Anto Papic on the road and that they would be going up to their place to see what was happening, whether they knew what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you were in the house. Did Anto Bralo and Franjo Kovac move over?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, we were in Finka's house and we saw Frano Kovac and Anto Bralo moving, and Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic, and we saw that Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic were moving towards Nikola Omazic's house, whereas Frano and Anto Bralo went towards Anto Bralo's house, that is to say, towards the stable. You come to the stable first, and they stopped there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Anto Bralo and Franjo Kovac, did they take the field or did they take the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: No, they took the road towards this depression where the stable is as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What about in front of the stable? Could Anto Papic see them, or Drago Josipovic, could they see them or not?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, they could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But they could also not see them; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, they could not see them too, depending on where they were standing. I don't know where they had taken shelter, whether they went right behind the stable or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But they went in different directions, in opposite directions?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, Anto Bralo and Frano Kovac went downwards whereas Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic went upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That is, before they met.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: If they met at all.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, tell us: Did they meet or did they not meet?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Would you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that Anto Bralo and Franjo Kovac went towards Anto Papic's stable whereas Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic went in the direction of Nikola Omazic's house, taking the road that way. Did they meet on the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: No, they could not have met because they went in opposite directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you were in Anto Bralo's house. Did you see who Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic met on the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Perhaps out of curiosity, Finka and I happened to look out of the window. We looked out of the window of Finka Bralo's house, and we saw that Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic met a group of women.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And children.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What happened then; did you see where they moved off to?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, we were interested in seeing who they met and where they were going, but we couldn't recognise whom they had met, but we saw that Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic left with those women and children towards Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, where that meeting took place between Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic with the Muslims, that is to say, near Nikola Omazic's house, in that vicinity?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I mean where they met.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, they met up above Nikola Omazic's house or -- the nearest house was Nikola Omazic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was that towards the road and the gate towards the yard?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: You mean the main road? No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Nikola Omazic's house is right by the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1993, did you happen to see any other Muslims?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know who else of the Muslims came to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: To the house of Anto Papic? Well, there was [redacted] with her husband [redacted] and her daughter-in-law and their three children; I saw Zilka [redacted] with her husband Cazim and his son Amir and Zenur, the other son, and his wife and two children. I also saw [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were there other Muslims in Anto Papic's house who were refugees?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, there was an old woman there too, and I know that she was a refugee from Prijedor and that she was put up in Fatima [redacted] old house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In addition to the Muslims in Anto Papic's house, were there Croats there as well?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: In Anto Papic's house there was Papic's family, his sister. She's a very old lady. His wife was there and her two children, and Anto Papic's wife was ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you tell us, please, once again how many Muslims there were in Anto Papic's house and how many Croats, or tell us the total number of people who were there?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to see and judge, there were five Croats, that is to say, his wife, his sister and the children, and 27 or 28 Muslims, which makes a total of about 32 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you go to Anto Papic's house on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, did I.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: It was about 10.30 when I arrived at Anto Papic's house. I went there because Fatima came to Anto Bralo's house, and she was there with us, and she said that Fahran had died, and we were all very sorry, and she told us that Fahran's children were poorly clothed. So I went at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That was at Anto Bralo's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: And when Fatima told me -- I went to Anto Papic's. It was half past ten. I took two trainers belonging to my son, sweat-shirts. My son was smaller, but I thought these clothes might come in handy, these track suits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know how these Muslims came to be in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mentioned Cazim Ramic. How did he happen to be there with his people?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: I didn't see Cazim Ramic personally, but I saw him when I was in the house. So I don't know how he, Cazim, that is, with his family got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And what about the Osmancevics?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: I know how the Osmancevics came there. Saiba, with her children, started out towards Anto Papic's house, and with her husband as well, and when she enter the house she saw that there were a lot of people there, a lot of refugees, and she continued on along -- continued towards Rovna with her children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who with?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: I think she went on her own. She was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are you certain or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't know how she went to Rovna, but I do know that her husband, some 15 or 20 minutes later, went to Rovna and rang us up at Anto Bralo's house for Franjo Kovac and Anto Bralo to go to Jozo Cerkez's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. We seem to have missed a step in this description. You said the women and children of Mirsad Osmancevic had gone to Rovna; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: After that do you know how Mirsad Osmancevic went to Rovan?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Mirsa Osmancevic went to Rovna with Drago Josipovic. Drago Josipovic gave Mirsad a vest and he went to Rovna. Drago came back to us and Mirsad stayed at Jozo Cerkez's house. Saiba went to see whether Jozo would take her in, and when he said he would, her husband turned up. While I was in Anto Bralo's house, Mirsad telephoned --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Let's make a break here and pause so that the interpreters can catch up.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Mirsad rang us up, because he said he didn't dare come from Rovna alone. Jozo Cerkez was threatened, that is, because he had taken Mirsad in, because everybody knew that Mirsad belonged to the BH army. Mirsad then called Franjo Kovac and Anto Bralo to come and fetch him. They weren't there. We told Mirsad they weren't there because they had gone out to feed Marija Papic's livestock.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, in the afternoon. When they returned from Marija Papic's house, they told us that Mirsad had telephoned and they wanted to go to Rovna but Mirsad had already arrived with his wife and children to Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you whether Anto Papic and his family took them in immediately.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that at Rovna, in Jozo Cerkez's house, Mirsad Omazic was there with his children?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us who threatened them? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know, but somebody did threaten them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When Mirsad Osmancevic came back in the evening --

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it was towards evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: -- and when he told you that they had been threatened, were any of you frightened? Were you afraid?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Of course we were afraid, because we were protecting a member of the BH army. Jozo Cerkez was threatened precisely for that reason, because that individual was put up in his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you feel that Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic were nervous in any way?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Anto Papic kept saying that he was afraid and Drago did too, but what could we do? The man was there with his wife and his three little children, and Drago said that they should stay in Anto Papic's house because they were all Muslims and so it was better they stick together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When Drago Josipovic left with Mirsad Osmancevic and went to Novna, you said, do you know if he was -- if Drago Josipovic helped in him any other way, Mirsad Osmancevic, that is? Do you know whether he gave him his vest?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. He gave him a vest and that he left towards Rovna wearing a camouflage vest. That's what Mirsad told us. He said he had gone to -- he had been wearing Drago Josipovic's camouflage vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We have been mentioning Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic here today. Will you tell us what Drago Josipovic looked like on that particular day? What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic was wearing a vest, an army vest, and jeans.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it a camouflage vest?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he carry a rifle?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know anything about how [redacted] reached Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. [redacted] came accompanied by Jozo Livancic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to Anto Papic's house, towards my own house, toward Nikola Omazic's house, because I had some livestock to tend to as well, and I saw Jozo leading [redacted], her mother, and their two children. There seems to be something wrong with my headset. They're falling off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know who went to fetch [redacted] to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: On the next day, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the 17th.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: I heard about this. I didn't see it, but I heard that Drago Josipovic had been asked by Fatima to go and fetch her, Fatima [redacted], that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: To bring them?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, to fetch them. Fatima told me that when she came to my house to use the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said you saw the meeting between Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic with Fatima [redacted] and her family?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How did Drago Josipovic behave on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: I couldn't see Drago immediately. I did see him meet up with them, but I couldn't see his face and his behaviour towards Fatima, but Fatima told me that Drago had cried because of Fahran. He was very sorry to learn of Fahran, and that she liked Drago very much, and that Drago is a very good man. When she came to use the telephone --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We're talking about Fatima. We said that Fatima was in Anto Bralo's house. That's right; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did she also go to Nikola Omazic's house that day?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Tell us how that came about.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: When I was at Anto Papic's house, Fatima asked me whether she could use my telephone, because Anto Papic's house did not have a telephone. I told Fatima that she could come to my house, that is to say, to Nikola Omazic's house, whenever she wanted to and use the phone whenever she wanted to. So she came to call up her other son Nevzudin in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Her other son. The son that was alive?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. And told him that had Fahran had died, and Nevzudin asked whether Drago was there and whether Drago could help her in any way, and I heard her telling her son Nevza that had Drago known of this conflict, he would have helped and saved her son.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How long did Fatima stay in your house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: She was with me for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you have a cigarette, have some coffee?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: We were sitting down and she had a smoke. I am not a smoker.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And after that, that day, did you meet again?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Fatima came to my house on the 17th. On the 17th, she came to ask whether she could call her son in Memso, in Vitez, to tell him that they were leaving Anto Papic's house and moving over to UNPROFOR, that is, that UNPROFOR would take them over from Anto Papic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did she say -- did she mention Drago Josipovic again?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. That morning she did mention Drago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he helping her again?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. She told me that Drago had drawn her attention a number of times to be careful because after that first conflict a bomb was thrown into the house of another Muslim, of Mehmed Alic, that they had to take care, there were all sorts of people. So they should really take care and not to move about very much and to move around warily.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So it was a suggestion made in good faith.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Fatima describe him in a favourable light or not?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Fatima always painted him in a very favourable light and said she loved him as if he were her own son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, we should adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Susak, could he tell us if the third witness on the list is still on the list, or is he coming tomorrow or during this week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, could you tell us tomorrow if you are calling Mr. Pranjkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, I intend to. He'll be here tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So we'll adjourn now.
